prompted_by: Main requested isolation of a precise edge/marginal/fiber consequence beyond the already identified local-projection and rank-five prior work, before any new broad packet.
important_additional_prior_art: The general edge/marginal lemma in the earlier packet is ALSO already contained in stronger form in Horodecki–Lewenstein–Vidal–Cirac, arXiv:quant-ph/0002089v1, https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0002089v1, Section II Lemmas 1–2. For an MxN PPT state with M-1 independent vectors |a_i,f> in the kernel, Lemma 1 gives either all |a_i,f> in the kernel or a product vector and its partial conjugate in the respective ranges; Lemma 2 constructs a PPT-preserving product subtraction and lowers the local support. Thus, if the opposite marginal is full rank and the state is PPT edge, the first alternative and the subtraction are both impossible. This is exactly the edge/codimension-one marginal implication, not a new lemma. Skowronek, arXiv:1105.2709v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1105.2709v1, Lemma 3.3 explicitly states a related 3xn special case and cites the 2000 result; its printed statement has a 3x3/3xn wording inconsistency, so the 2000 general lemma is the cleaner primary source.
already_known_components: Chen–Yang–Tang, arXiv:1609.05100v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1609.05100v1, Lemma 15(i),(ii),(v) already gives the local-projection Schmidt-number inequality/lift and PPT separable-cut consequence; Lemma 33(iii) gives rank>=5 for a PPT state with bipartite Schmidt number>=3. Chen–Djokovic, arXiv:1301.2372v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1301.2372v1, Proposition 5(i) gives rank greater than max local ranks for PPT entanglement. Yang–Leung–Tang, arXiv:1603.03534v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1603.03534v1, Corollary 3.6 gives 3x3 PPT Schmidt number<=2. None of these components should be called newly discovered.
precise_remaining_conditional_synthesis: For a bipartite PPT edge state rho of full local ranks m<=n and Schmidt number>=3, let r=rank(rho), s=rank(rho^Gamma). Every codimension-one projection on the m-dimensional side has full local ranks (m-1,n), remains PPT and entangled, and has rank and partial-transpose rank at least n+1. Therefore, for every nonzero a in C^m, dim(range(rho) intersect (span(a) tensor C^n))<=r-(n+1), and the analogous bound holds for rho^Gamma with s. In particular, if r=n+1, range(rho) is a completely entangled subspace; if s=n+1, range(rho^Gamma) is. For the original 4x4 target's extreme full-local branch, n=4 and the rank-five conclusion follows. For a (3,4) extreme branch, every rank-two cut of the 3-side has local ranks (2,4) and is PPT entangled of Schmidt number 2; every rank-three cut of the 4-side is full-local 3x3 PPT entangled and has Schmidt number 2. These statements are proposed as an explicitly sourced combination, not a proven-new result or a 4x4 solution.
